question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: This initial construction activity involves the removal of vegetation and debris, while preserving designated objects.
explanation: Clearing and grubbing removes vegetation and debris while preserving designated objects.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: The professional responsible for establishing the limits of work and designating which trees and shrubs must remain.
explanation: The Engineer establishes work limits and designates which trees/shrubs remain.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: The contractual party responsible for preserving all objects designated to remain undamaged during vegetation removal.
explanation: The Contractor preserves designated objects undamaged during vegetation removal.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: The specified type of paint required for treating cut or scarred surfaces on trees that are to be retained.
explanation: Asphalt base paint is required for treating cut or scarred surfaces on retained trees.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: The required minimum coverage depth of earth for the top layer of buried debris to ensure a pleasing appearance.
explanation: Buried debris requires minimum 300 mm earth cover for pleasing appearance.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: The maximum permitted height above ground for stumps left outside grading limits in non-excavation areas.
explanation: Maximum stump height left outside grading limits is 150 mm above ground.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: The required method for debris placement when burial is used for disposal, to prevent void spaces.
explanation: Debris for burial must be placed in layers to prevent void spaces.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: Woody material may be disposed of by this process, and the resulting product can be used for mulch or slope erosion control.
explanation: Chipping woody material produces mulch for erosion control.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: Wood chips used as mulch for slope erosion control shall have a maximum thickness and a limit on individual face surface area.
explanation: Wood chips as mulch are specifically for slope erosion control with thickness limits.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: Trees identified as having this condition shall be buried or disposed of as specifically directed by the Engineer.
explanation: Diseased trees must be buried or disposed of as directed by the Engineer.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: Branches of trees extending over the roadbed shall be trimmed to provide this above the roadbed surface.
explanation: Branches over roadbed must be trimmed to provide clear height above surface.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: This category of excavation includes all materials not classified under other specific pay items in the Bill of Quantities.
explanation: Unclassified excavation includes materials not under other pay items.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: This type of excavation consists of igneous, sedimentary, and metamorphic rocks that require blasting or rippers for removal.
explanation: Rock excavation involves rocks requiring blasting or rippers for removal.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: This classification includes all excavation work not falling under rock excavation or other specific categories in the Bill of Quantities.
explanation: Common excavation includes work not under rock or other specific categories.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: This type involves removing saturated or unsaturated mixtures of soils and organic matter unsuitable for foundation material.
explanation: Muck excavation removes organic matter mixtures unsuitable for foundations.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: This type of excavation involves obtaining approved material from specific sources for use in embankment construction.
explanation: Borrow excavation obtains approved material from specific sources for embankments.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: When discrepancies exist between actual elevations and the plans, this survey must be conducted before construction begins.
explanation: Pre-construction survey is required when actual elevations differ from plans.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: The reference plane used for the pre-construction survey that matches the approved plan.
explanation: Datum plane matches the approved plan reference for pre-construction survey.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: The required surface condition for all completed excavation work.
explanation: Completed excavation work requires smooth and uniform surface condition.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: The required preliminary work that must be completed in an area before any excavation can begin.
explanation: Clearing and grubbing must be completed before excavation begins.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: This valuable soil layer must be removed and stored separately when encountered in excavation or embankment areas.
explanation: Topsoil must be removed and stored separately when encountered.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: The professional who determines the extent and depth for removal of this valuable surface material.
explanation: The Engineer determines extent and depth for topsoil removal.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: The specific application of suitable excavated material for supporting structural foundations.
explanation: Bedding uses suitable excavated material to support structural foundations.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: The classification given to soil that cannot achieve proper compaction density in embankments.
explanation: Unsuitable soil cannot achieve proper compaction density in embankments.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: The specific type of excavation material that should not be used until readily accessible roadway excavation is placed.
explanation: Borrow excavation material should not be used until roadway excavation is placed.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: This preparatory process involves adding moisture to excavation areas and borrow pits before material removal.
explanation: Pre-watering adds moisture to excavation areas before material removal.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: The required depth of moisture penetration when using this preparatory watering technique.
explanation: Pre-watering requires full depth moisture penetration.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: The equipment required to verify adequate moisture penetration throughout the excavation depth.
explanation: Drilling equipment verifies adequate moisture penetration throughout excavation depth.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: The mobile equipment used to supplement moisture levels in embankment materials during compaction.
explanation: Truck watering units supplement moisture levels in embankment materials during compaction.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: This controlled blasting technique is required for rock excavation involving drilling and shooting.
explanation: Presplitting is required for rock excavation involving drilling and shooting.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: The required timing for detonating the explosive charges in this rock excavation method.
explanation: Explosive charges must be detonated simultaneously in presplitting.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: The initial project section where this rock-breaking method must be tested and approved before full-scale operations.
explanation: Test section is where rock-breaking method is tested before full-scale operations.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: The maximum sieve size, in millimeters, that stemming material must pass through for proper confinement of explosives.
explanation: Stemming material must pass through 9.5 mm sieve for proper explosive confinement.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: The required maintenance period for all excavated ditches until project handover.
explanation: Excavated ditches must be maintained until final acceptance.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: The specified placement for loose materials removed during furrow ditch cleaning.
explanation: Loose materials from furrow ditch cleaning must be placed on downhill side.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: The required depth, in millimeters, for excavating rock below the subgrade level within the roadbed limits.
explanation: Rock must be excavated 150 mm below subgrade level within roadbed limits.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: The required treatment for undrained pockets left in rock surfaces after excavation.
explanation: Undrained pockets in rock surfaces must be properly drained.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: The process of breaking up material below subgrade to a specified depth to prepare for compaction.
explanation: Scarifying breaks up material below subgrade to prepare for compaction.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: The required condition for these material sites after excavation to allow accurate volume measurement.
explanation: Material sites must be bladed and shaped after excavation for accurate volume measurement.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: The required condition for any fencing that must be temporarily removed during material extraction operations.
explanation: Temporarily removed fencing must be replaced as original.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: The responsibility of the Contractor regarding animals when fence portions are removed from these sites.
explanation: Contractor must confine livestock when fence portions are removed.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: The specific material type requiring careful excavation to prevent entrapment in backfill areas.
explanation: Muck requires careful excavation to prevent entrapment in backfill areas.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: The critical step required before placing backfill in areas where unsuitable material was removed.
explanation: Cross-sectional measurements are required before backfilling unsuitable material removal areas.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: These temporary enclosures are built to keep water out of foundation excavations and must be removed afterward.
explanation: Cribs and cofferdams are temporary enclosures to keep water out of excavations.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: The required notification to the Engineer before beginning any excavation for structures.
explanation: Engineer must be notified sufficiently in advance before structure excavation.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: Materials like boulders and logs encountered during structure excavation that must be removed from the site.
explanation: Objectionable materials like boulders and logs must be removed from site.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: The status of footing elevations shown on plans, which are considered as this until verified or changed by the Engineer.
explanation: Footing elevations on plans are approximate only until verified by Engineer.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: The required surface preparation for rock foundations, which can be level, stepped, or serrated as directed.
explanation: Rock foundations require firm surface preparation (level, stepped, or serrated).

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: The process of filling seams or crevices in rock foundations to ensure structural integrity.
explanation: Grouting fills seams or crevices in rock foundations for structural integrity.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: For structures other than pipe culverts, the required sequence of operations when foundation piles are used.
explanation: Excavate first, then drive foundation piles for non-culvert structures.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: For pipe culverts, the required minimum additional width of the trench beyond the pipe's outside diameter.
explanation: Pipe culvert trenches require minimum 300 mm additional width beyond pipe outside diameter.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: These temporary enclosures must be used where water-bearing strata are encountered above the excavation bottom.
explanation: Cofferdams are required where water-bearing strata are above excavation bottom.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: For cofferdams, this concrete element may be required to resist uplift when dewatering before placing the footing is impractical.
explanation: Foundation seal resists uplift when dewatering before footing placement is impractical.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: The required characteristic for cofferdams regarding their ability to prevent water ingress.
explanation: Cofferdams must be practically watertight to prevent water ingress.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: The required action for cofferdams that tilt or move during installation to ensure proper clearance.
explanation: Tilted or moved cofferdams must be righted or enlarged for proper clearance.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: For structures other than pipe culverts, backfill material must be this type of granular material to ensure proper drainage.
explanation: Backfill for non-culvert structures must be free draining granular material.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: For structures other than pipe culverts, the maximum thickness, in millimeters, for placing backfill in horizontal layers.
explanation: Backfill horizontal layers maximum thickness is 150 mm for non-culvert structures.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: The required equipment for compacting backfill layers around structures other than pipe culverts.
explanation: Mechanical tampers are required for compacting backfill around non-culvert structures.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: The required waiting period, in days, before placing significantly higher backfill on one side of a masonry structure.
explanation: Wait 14 days before placing higher backfill on one side of masonry structure.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: This category includes materials like peat, muck, and soils with excessive liquid limits or plasticity indices that cannot be used in embankments.
explanation: Unsuitable materials include peat, muck, and soils with excessive limits not usable in embankments.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: The required preliminary work that must be completed before any embankment construction begins.
explanation: Clearing and grubbing must be completed before embankment construction begins.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: The specific material type that is prohibited in embankment areas where piling will be installed.
explanation: Unsuitable materials are prohibited in embankment areas where piling will be installed.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: The required compaction depth, in millimeters, for the existing ground surface before embankment placement when specified.
explanation: Existing ground surface requires 150 mm compaction depth before embankment placement.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: The required maximum loose layer thickness, in millimeters, for placing earth material in roadway embankments.
explanation: Maximum loose layer thickness for earth material in embankments is 200 mm.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: The required ground treatment for embankments less than 1.2 meters high, involving removal of vegetation and soil breaking.
explanation: Embankments under 1.2 m require sod removal and scarifying.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: The construction technique required for steep slopes exceeding 3:1 when placing embankments.
explanation: Benching is required for steep slopes exceeding 3:1 when placing embankments.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: The maximum rock content percentage that allows standard placement in 200mm layers without special procedures.
explanation: Maximum 25% rock content allows standard 200mm layer placement without special procedures.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: Before commencing the formation of embankments, proposals for the compaction of each type of fill material, types of compaction equipment, number of passes required, and the method of adjusting moisture content to be used in the Works shall be submitted by the Contractor to this person for approval.
explanation: Compaction proposals must be submitted to the Engineer for approval.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: Throughout the periods when compaction of earthworks is in progress, the Contractor shall adhere to the procedures found from these for each type of material.
explanation: Contractor must adhere to procedures from compaction trials for each material type.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: Material placed in all embankment layer and the material scarified to the designated depth below sub-grade in cut sections shall be compacted by the Contractor until uniform density of not less than this percentage of the maximum determined by AASHTO T 99, Method C is attained.
explanation: Compacted density must be at least 95% of maximum determined by AASHTO T 99, Method C.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: During progress of the Work, density tests of compacted material shall be made by the Engineer in accordance with AASHTO T 191, ASTM D 2167, or other approved field density test, including the use of these.
explanation: Density tests may include nuclear testing devices.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: Embankment materials classified as rock shall be deposited, spread and leveled the full width of the fill with sufficient earth or other fine material so deposited to fill these to produce a dense compact embankment.
explanation: Fine material must fill interstices in rock embankment materials.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: Adjustments in slopes shall be made to avoid injury in standing trees or marring of weathered rock, or to harmonize with existing landscape features, and the transition to such adjusted slope shall be gradual. At intersections of cut and fills, slopes shall be adjusted and warped to flow into each other or into the natural ground surfaces without noticeable break.
explanation: Slopes shall be adjusted and warped to flow into each other without noticeable break.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: After the roadbed has been substantially completed, the full width shall be conditioned by removing any soft or other unstable material that will not compact properly or serve the intended purpose.
explanation: Finishing roadbed and slopes involves removing unstable material after roadbed completion.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: The finished compacted surface of the subgrade shall conform to the allowable tolerances as specified.
explanation: Finished subgrade must conform to specified subgrade level tolerances.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: All materials below subgrade level in earth cuts to a depth 150 mm or other depth shown in the Plans or as directed by the Engineer shall be excavated.
explanation: Subgrade in common excavation requires removal of materials 150 mm below subgrade level.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: This consists of authorized hauling in excess of the free-haul distance.
explanation: Overhaul is authorized hauling beyond free-haul distance.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: This is the specified distance that excavated material shall be hauled without additional compensation.
explanation: Free-haul distance is the specified haul distance without additional compensation.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: The maximum compacted thickness of one layer shall not exceed this.
explanation: Maximum compacted layer thickness is 150 mm.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: Compacting shall progress gradually from the side to the center, parallel to this.
explanation: Compacting shall progress parallel to the centerline.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: It shall consist of any combination of gravel, sand, silt and clay or other approved combination of materials free from vegetable or other objectionable matter.
explanation: Soil aggregate consists of gravel, sand, silt, and clay free from objectionable matter.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: The hydrated lime shall be uniformly spread using either the dry or these methods.
explanation: Hydrated lime can be spread using dry or slurry (wet) methods.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: Dry lime should not be spread under these conditions to avoid excessive dust.
explanation: Dry lime should not be spread in windy conditions to avoid excessive dust.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: For uniform distribution of dry lime, this type of equipment is preferable.
explanation: Approved spreader is preferable for uniform dry lime distribution.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: The mixing process for lime stabilization. After the last lime application and partial mixing, the entire mass of the mixture shall be placed in this formation on the road surface for further mixing.
explanation: Lime stabilization mixture shall be placed in windrow formation for further mixing.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: The equipment for spreading lime stabilized material. The material shall be spread by a self-propelled pneumatic-tire blade grader or one of these.
explanation: Lime stabilized material can be spread by mechanical spreader.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: The required field density. Compaction shall continue until a field density of not less than ________ of the compacted maximum dry density has been attained.
explanation: Compaction shall continue until 100% of compacted maximum dry density is attained.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: Protection, Curing and Maintenance requirements. After finishing, the lime-stabilized base course surface must be protected against rapid drying for at least five days using approved methods.
explanation: Curing methods protect lime-stabilized base course from rapid drying for at least five days.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: Protection, Curing and Maintenance requirements. One curing method involves covering the completed surface with a layer of earth or sand and maintaining it in this condition.
explanation: Curing with earth or sand cover requires maintaining moist condition.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: Protection, Curing and Maintenance requirements. An alternative curing method is to maintain the surface in a thorough and continuously moist condition by doing this.
explanation: Sprinkling with water maintains continuous moist condition for curing.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: Proportioning of Mixture for Portland cement stabilization. The exact percentage of cement to be added shall be fixed by this person on the basis of preliminary laboratory tests.
explanation: Engineer fixes exact cement percentage based on preliminary laboratory tests.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: Proportioning of Mixture for Portland cement stabilization. The amount of cement to be added to the soil-aggregate is determined as a percentage of this material.
explanation: Cement amount is determined as percentage of dry soil.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: Travel Plant Method requirements. The salvaged or new soil-aggregate shall be pulverized until at least 80 mass percent of all material other than stone or gravel will pass this sieve size.
explanation: At least 80% must pass 4.75 mm (No. 4) sieve after pulverization.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: Travel Plant Method requirements. Any material retained on this sieve size and other unsuitable material shall be removed before mixing.
explanation: Material retained on 50 mm sieve shall be removed before mixing.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: Travel Plant Method requirements. The mixer shall be equipped with this device to introduce the required quantity of water during the mixing cycle.
explanation: Mixer must have water metering device for introducing required water quantity.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: This method involves pulverizing soil-aggregate, placing it in windrows, applying cement, and mixing with a mobile plant that travels along the road.
explanation: Travel Plant Method uses mobile plant that travels along road.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: This method involves proportioning and mixing soil-aggregate with cement and water in a fixed location plant equipped with feeding and metering devices.
explanation: Central Plant Method uses fixed location plant with feeding and metering devices.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: Protection, Curing and Maintenance for cement treated base. The completed base shall be cured with this type of seal applied after final rolling.
explanation: Cement treated base shall be cured with bituminous curing seal after final rolling.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: Portland Cement requirements. Cement which has become partially set or contains lumps of caked cement will receive this action.
explanation: Partially set or lumpy cement shall be rejected.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: It shall consist of natural sand, stone screenings or other inert materials with similar characteristics, having hard, strong and durable particles.
explanation: Fine aggregate consists of natural sand or stone screenings with hard, durable particles.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: This is the maximum allowable percentage of material that can pass the 0.075 mm sieve by washing.
explanation: Maximum 3% of fine aggregate can pass 0.075 mm sieve by washing.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: If a fine aggregate produces a color darker than the standard in a specific test, it shall be rejected.
explanation: Color darker than standard in colorimatic test causes fine aggregate rejection.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: Coarse aggregate must be free from any of these, which are undesirable layers of material sticking to the pieces.
explanation: Coarse aggregate must be free from adherent coatings.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: This is the maximum allowable mass percentage of material passing the 0.075 mm (No. 200) sieve in coarse aggregate.
explanation: Maximum 1% of coarse aggregate can pass 0.075 mm sieve.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: According to Table 20, what is the required appearance for a questionable water supply to be acceptable?
explanation: Questionable water supply must be clear to be acceptable.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: According to Table 20, what is the required odor for a questionable water supply to be acceptable?
explanation: Questionable water supply must be odorless to be acceptable.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: According to Table 20, what is the required color for a questionable water supply to be acceptable?
explanation: Questionable water supply must be colorless to be acceptable.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: According to Table 20, what physical property must show no marked change in its final set when testing a questionable water supply?
explanation: Time of setting must show no marked change in final set.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: This type of bar, which must be deformed, is used to hold adjacent concrete slabs together.
explanation: Tie bars (deformed) hold adjacent concrete slabs together.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: This type of bar, which is plain and round, is used for load transfer across joints.
explanation: Dowels (plain and round) are used for load transfer across joints.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: The are called laminated sacks, sheeting films, or any equivalent material that protects the concrete during curing.
explanation: Curing covers (laminated sacks, sheeting films) protect concrete during curing.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: In Proportioning, Consistency and Strength of Concrete. It is the intent of this Standard to require approximately this many bags of cement per cubic meter of concrete.
explanation: Standard requires approximately nine bags of cement per cubic meter of concrete.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: In Proportioning, Consistency and Strength of Concrete. The standard requirement of approximately nine bags of cement per cubic meter is based on a bag weight of this many kilograms.
explanation: Standard requirement based on 40 kg cement bags.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Ruminant Lairage: These structural elements are mandated to physically separate groups of ruminants from different batches, with their height being dependent on the animal size.
explanation: Gates separate ruminant groups from different batches with height dependent on animal size.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Ruminant Lairage: The minimum required height for a wall divider intended to separate groups of large ruminants, such as cattle, is specified as this exact measurement.
explanation: Wall divider minimum height for large ruminants (cattle) is 1.5 m.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Ruminant Lairage: For smaller animals like goats and sheep, the standard sets a lower minimum height for the wall divider, which is this specific measurement.
explanation: Wall divider minimum height for small ruminants (goats, sheep) is 1.2 m.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: It is the minimum height that an FMR embankment must be raised above the flood level of the area.
explanation: FMR embankment must be raised 0.6 m above flood level.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: The number of primary types into which roadside barriers are classified.
explanation: Roadside barriers are classified into three primary types.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: The recommended location for a barrier relative to the edge of the shoulder.
explanation: Barriers should be located beyond the edge of the shoulder.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: The number of primary method steps listed for performing this rock excavation technique.
explanation: Rock excavation technique uses 3 primary method steps.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: For structures other than pipe culverts, the required layer thickness, in millimeters, for placing and compacting foundation fill material.
explanation: Foundation fill layer thickness for non-culvert structures is 150 mm.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: What is the minimum required relative strength percentage at 7 and 28 days for mortar when testing the effect of organic impurities?
explanation: Minimum relative strength at 7 and 28 days for mortar is 95%.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: According to Table 21, what is the minimum slump value, in mm, allowed for concrete that is vibrated?
explanation: Minimum slump for vibrated concrete is 10 mm.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: According to Table 21, what is the maximum slump value, in mm, allowed for concrete that is not vibrated?
explanation: Maximum slump for non-vibrated concrete is 75 mm.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: According to Table 21, what is the required compressive strength, in MPa, for the concrete?
explanation: Required concrete compressive strength is 24.1 MPa.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: The are called laminated sacks, sheeting films, or any equivalent material that protects the concrete during curing.
explanation: Curing covers (laminated sacks, sheeting films) protect concrete during curing.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: What is the minimum required gap, in millimeters, that must be maintained between the end of the sleeve and the end of the dowel bar?
explanation: Minimum gap between sleeve end and dowel bar end is 25 mm.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: According to the specifications, what is the required length, in millimeters, that a dowel sleeve must cover?
explanation: Dowel sleeve must cover 50 mm ± 5 mm.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: According to Table 20, what is the minimum required compressive strength percentage of the control at 7 days for a questionable water supply?
explanation: Minimum compressive strength at 7 days is 90% of control.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: According to Table 20, what is the maximum allowable deviation for the time of setting, where it can be set later than the control?
explanation: Maximum allowable setting time deviation later than control is 1 hour 30 minutes.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: According to Table 20, what is the maximum allowable limit for total solids, in parts per million?
explanation: Maximum allowable total solids is 500 ppm.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: According to Table 20, if the upper limit is 8.5 pH, what is the lower limit of the acceptable pH range for a questionable water supply?
explanation: Acceptable pH range for questionable water supply is 4.5 to 8.5.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: If the coarse aggregate is subjected to five cycles of the sodium sulfate soundness test, the weighted loss shall not exceed ______
explanation: Weighted loss after five cycles sodium sulfate test shall not exceed 12%.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: What is the maximum permitted mass percentage of clay lumps allowed in a coarse aggregate?
explanation: Maximum clay lumps in coarse aggregate is 0.25% by mass.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: What is the maximum permitted mass percentage of soft fragments allowed in a coarse aggregate?
explanation: Maximum soft fragments in coarse aggregate is 3.5% by mass.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: What is the maximum allowable mass percent of wear for coarse aggregate when tested by AASHTO T 96?
explanation: Maximum wear for coarse aggregate by AASHTO T 96 is 40%.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: What is the minimum required density, in kg/m³, for blast furnace slag used as a coarse aggregate?
explanation: Blast furnace slag coarse aggregate minimum density is 1120 kg/m³.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: According to Table 18, what is the specified range, as a mass percent passing, for the 4.75 mm (No. 4) sieve?
explanation: Mass percent passing 4.75 mm sieve is 95-100%.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: According to Table 18, what is the specified range, as a mass percent passing, for the 1.18 mm (No. 16) sieve?
explanation: Mass percent passing 1.18 mm sieve is 45-80%.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: According to Table 18, what is the specified range, as a mass percent passing, for the 0.300 mm (No. 50) sieve?
explanation: Mass percent passing 0.300 mm sieve is 5-30%.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: According to Table 18, what is the specified range, as a mass percent passing, for the 0.150 mm (No. 100) sieve?
explanation: Mass percent passing 0.150 mm sieve is 0-10%.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: According to the standard, for how many days is the relative strength of the mortar compared to evaluate the effect of organic impurities?
explanation: Relative mortar strength is compared at 7 and 28 days for organic impurities effect.

question_text: BONUS: Magiging Engineer ka, Bayaw!
explanation: Stay positive and claim your success as an engineer!

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: What is the sieve number used to determine the maximum allowable percentage of fine material by washing?
explanation: Sieve No. 200 is used to determine maximum allowable fine material by washing.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: What is the maximum allowable weighted loss percentage for a fine aggregate subjected to five cycles of the sodium sulfate soundness test?
explanation: Maximum weighted loss for fine aggregate sodium sulfate test is 10%.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: What is the maximum permitted mass percentage of shale allowed in a fine aggregate?
explanation: Maximum shale in fine aggregate is 1% by mass.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: What is the maximum permitted mass percentage of clay lumps allowed in a fine aggregate?
explanation: Maximum clay lumps in fine aggregate is 1% by mass.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: According to Table 17, what cement type number is recommended for massive structures such as dams?
explanation: Type IV cement is recommended for massive structures such as dams.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: According to Table 17, what number of cement type specifically mentioned for use in cold weather concreting?
explanation: Type III cement is specifically for cold weather concreting.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: According to Table 17, the maximum C3A content, as a percentage, for Type II Portland Cement?
explanation: Maximum C3A content for Type II Portland Cement is 8%.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: According to Table 17, the maximum C3A content, as a percentage, for Type V Portland Cement?
explanation: Maximum C3A content for Type V Portland Cement is 5%.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: According to Table 17, the maximum C3S content, as a percentage, for Type IV Portland Cement?
explanation: Maximum C3S content for Type IV Portland Cement is 50%.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: According to Table 17, what number of cement type specifically recommended for use in pavements?
explanation: Type I cement is specifically recommended for use in pavements.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: According to Table 17, what number of cement type classified primarily for moderate sulfate resistance?
explanation: Type II cement is classified primarily for moderate sulfate resistance.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: Portland Cement requirements. The minimum 7-day compressive strength, in MPa, for mortar sample acceptance.
explanation: Minimum 7-day compressive strength for mortar acceptance is 23.46 MPa.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: Portland Cement requirements. The 28-day compressive strength requirement, in MPa, that the 7-day strength is compared to.
explanation: 28-day compressive strength requirement is 27.6 MPa.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: Portland Cement requirements. The percentage of the 28-day strength that the 7-day strength must achieve for acceptance.
explanation: 7-day strength must achieve 85% of 28-day strength for acceptance.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: Protection, Curing and Maintenance for cement treated base. The minimum number of days the curing seal film must be maintained.
explanation: Curing seal film must be maintained for minimum 5 days.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: Protection, Curing and Maintenance for cement treated base. The maximum application rate for the bituminous curing seal, in liters per square meter.
explanation: Maximum bituminous curing seal application rate is 1.00 L/m².

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: Protection, Curing and Maintenance for cement treated base. The minimum application rate for the bituminous curing seal, in liters per square meter.
explanation: Minimum bituminous curing seal application rate is 0.5 L/m².

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: Travel Plant Method requirements. The maximum time allowed, in hours, for wet mixing, laydown, and finishing.
explanation: Maximum time for wet mixing, laydown, and finishing is 2 hours.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: Travel Plant Method requirements. The minimum mass percent of material (excluding stone/gravel) that must pass the 4.75 mm sieve after pulverization.
explanation: Minimum 80% of material (excluding stone/gravel) must pass 4.75 mm sieve after pulverization.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: Proportioning of Mixture for Portland cement stabilization. The minimum cement content, as a mass percentage of dry soil.
explanation: Minimum cement content for Portland cement stabilization is 6% of dry soil mass.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: Proportioning of Mixture for Portland cement stabilization. The maximum cement content, as a mass percentage of dry soil.
explanation: Maximum cement content for Portland cement stabilization is 10% of dry soil mass.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: Protection, Curing and Maintenance requirements. The minimum curing period, in days, for lime-stabilized base course.
explanation: Minimum curing period for lime-stabilized base course is 5 days.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: Protection, Curing and Maintenance requirements. The thickness, in millimeters, of the earth or sand layer used for curing.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: In mixing concrete, the concrete may be mixed at the site of the work in a ________________.
explanation: Concrete may be mixed either in central mixers or truck mixers at the site of work.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: When concrete are mixed at the Site or in a central mixing plant, the mixing time shall not be less than ___ seconds nor more than ___ seconds, unless mixer performance tests prove adequate mixing of the concrete is a shorter period.
explanation: Mixing time shall not be less than 50 seconds nor more than 90 seconds, unless mixer performance tests prove adequate mixing in a shorter period.

question_text: ____________ is a field test used to measure the consistency and plasticity of freshly mixed concrete by observing the vertical settlement of a conical specimen after the mold is lifted.
explanation: The slump test measures the consistency and plasticity of freshly mixed concrete by observing vertical settlement of a conical specimen.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: As per limitation of mixing, no concrete shall be mixed, placed or finished when ______________ is insufficient, unless an adequate and approved artificial lighting system is operated.
explanation: No concrete shall be mixed, placed or finished when natural light is insufficient, unless an adequate artificial lighting system is operated.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: During hot weather, the Engineer may require that steps be taken to prevent the temperature of mixed concrete from exceeding a maximum temperature of ____ degree C.
explanation: During hot weather, the temperature of mixed concrete shall not exceed 32°C.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: Concrete that is not placed within ____ minutes from the time the ingredients were charged into the mixing drum shall not be used.
explanation: Concrete not placed within 90 minutes from the time ingredients were charged into the mixing drum shall not be used.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: The minimum distance beyond each edge of the proposed concrete pavement that the trimming operation must extend.
explanation: Trimming operation must extend at least 75 cm beyond each edge of the proposed concrete pavement.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: The maximum thickness per layer for filling areas below established grade at the form line with approved granular materials.
explanation: The maximum thickness per layer for filling areas below established grade is 2 cm.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: Two specific properties of the concrete mixture that must be tested, witnessed by government personnel, according to the specifications.
explanation: Density and strength are the two properties of concrete mixture that must be tested and witnessed by government personnel.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: The action required if trimming operations result in a loss of density in the subgrade or base material.
explanation: If trimming operations result in loss of density, stabilizers shall be added.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: The required characteristic of the foundation under the forms to ensure they are firmly in contact for their whole length and at the specified grade.
explanation: The foundation under the forms must be hard and true to ensure firm contact for the whole length and at specified grade.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: The material specified for filling roadbed areas that are found below established grade at the form line.
explanation: Clay soil is specified for filling roadbed areas found below established grade at the form line.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: If traffic is allowed on the prepared subgrade, the surface must be checked and corrected at this specific time relative to concrete placement.
explanation: If traffic is allowed on prepared subgrade, the surface must be checked and corrected immediately ahead of concrete placement.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: The method specified for correcting imperfections or variations in the roadbed that are found above the established grade.
explanation: Imperfections or variations above established grade shall be corrected by tamping or cutting.

question_text: Agricultural Structures - Farm-to-Market Roads: Equipment must be at the jobsite sufficiently ahead of construction start for this specific purpose.
explanation: Equipment must be at the jobsite sufficiently ahead of construction start for examination and approval.
